queryKeyFactories.policy: The active-tenant root separates filtered lists, property/all counts, per-property counts of one queue, last-visit count, item details, notes, activity, Handling History, response-target policies, and target analytics. Per-property queue counts sit under the counts prefix, keyed by queue, so every counts invalidation after an Inbox command also refreshes the property section. An item's detail, notes, activity and Handling History are SIBLINGS keyed by aspect then item id, not descendants of the detail, so each is refreshed by name: the cache policy write-through patches a detail after a command (re-reading it only after a refused reply check) and invalidates notes and Handling History explicitly. The on-demand analysis poll invalidates one detail every few seconds while it waits for an analysis it requested (at most 90 s), which under the old nesting also refetched that item's mounted notes and Handling History each time; the property profile, reply-language and AI-access settings pages invalidate every detail, but no pane is mounted there, so under the old nesting that only marked notes and Handling History stale. Filters and item ids remain part of the cache identity. Response-target policy and analytics keys include either the globally unique Property id or the explicit Organization scope, preventing Property and Organization settings from sharing cache entries.

Every live subtree includes organizationId. Feed and settings are disjoint because bell refreshes must not evict settings; list identity includes limit/filter, head refreshes only the first page, and the email capability adds propertyId because admission is property-scoped.

Active-organization reads live under the identity root. Login, sign-out, and successful invitation acceptance clear the complete QueryClient at the confirmed session/tenant transition, so no unscoped identity or sibling context cache crosses tenants. Personal and organization invitation response shapes are disjoint siblings below the invitation prefix. The departing member's outstanding-responsibility worklist is a separate leaf under the same root: it describes the caller's current standing rather than the directory, is read at staleTime 0, and is invalidated by leave mutations alone. The per-property merchant AI consent snapshot is another leaf, keyed by the globally unique propertyId: the import flow's AI-analysis step reads it, a successful enable replaces it locally from the command result, and the AI settings route reads the same snapshot through its loader rather than through this key. The read-only Organization AI overview is a separate sibling leaf, not a parent of the per-property snapshots: it spans every Property the viewer may manage AI for, so any Merchant AI command or decision deferral must invalidate it explicitly alongside the affected property snapshot. The served Merchant AI notice is a third sibling leaf, independent of any Property: the import wizard's setup step reads it to render the consent ceremony, it changes only with a deploy, and a notice mismatch on a consent command is surfaced to the merchant rather than repaired from cache. The reporter's own beta-feedback history is a further leaf under the same root: it is scoped server-side by the caller's actor pseudonym rather than by any key argument, is read only while the dialog's reports panel is open, and is invalidated by a successful submission from that same dialog.

The list is active-tenant data; globally unique propertyId scopes detail data, and responsible managers descend from that detail so property-level invalidation includes the assignment projection. Per-Property setup steps descend from the same detail and the accessible setup summaries descend from the list, so every existing Property detail or list invalidation also refreshes the setup read derived from those facts.

Fleet is a real prefix above range-specific infinite entries. Staff/property callers include their property and view filters in the argument object. Google performance is isolated by property, preset, catalogue version, and view epoch; an authorization lease adds leaseRef beneath that exact report.

Trend, aggregate, and insights projections are independent property-scoped siblings under the AI root; insights also keys the selected day range, and globally unique propertyId prevents cross-property reuse. Review-analysis progress is another property-scoped sibling: it polls only while analysis is running and is invalidated when the property's AI authorization changes. Organization spend is the one organization-scoped leaf: a monthly amount read by the AI overview, stale after a minute and never mutated by the client.

Staff goals include propertyId, governed list callers include property/model filters in the argument object, and a detail includes both propertyId and goalId so a goal id cannot alias another property. Goal writes currently invalidate the family root. The live month-to-date progress of the goals that target one subject (a Portal Group's goal card) nests propertyId and the subject (`portal_group:<id>`) under the root, so a group id cannot alias another property; it is a display read that is never the monthly result, and goes stale on its own short staleTime.
Participation and accessible-portal projections are separate property-scoped siblings, allowing focused refresh while the family root remains available for full Staff teardown.
Staff activity and the reply-profile/template library are distinct propertyId-scoped projections beneath the Review root; neither can alias state from another property.

Property lists, groups, and goal-subject projections include propertyId. Every successful Portal Group create, rename, archive, member-add, or member-remove command goes through one named cache policy that invalidates the exact groups, goalSubjects, goalSubjectNames, and overview keys for that Property (the Portals overview names each Portal's group) and the results overview keys by prefix; failed commands do not run the policy. The Portals overview (every Portal of a Property, read in one batch) sits under the property prefix apart from the plain list, and its read is always refetched on arrival. Property-wide guest-experience data has its own propertyId prefix, and Portal-specific experience projections descend from it so a brand-profile write refreshes every affected screen. Detail descendants use globally unique portalId, while approved destinations remain Portal-scoped. The language coverage read (which wording each language has) descends from the Portal experience, so every Portal update, every Portal or Property wording write and every link edit refreshes it. What the New portal dialog reads about a Property (default languages, eligible managers) sits under the same prefix as creationOptions, is fetched only while the dialog is open, and is refreshed on each opening; a successful create invalidates the whole portals family, which includes the group keys, so a create that joins a group does not run the member-add policy. The Portals overview's results (one read per time range and comparison, under the property prefix) are a prefix invalidation in that policy: its root stands for every window, because the group a Portal is in decides which row it adds to. A group's own page (its history, under the group's id) is another: its per-Property root stands for every group of the Property, because a rename or a move shows in the group and in its ledger. The All properties page reads the same two projections for every Property the reader may use, so they have a subtree of their own (portalKeys.organizationOverview, and the results by time range and comparison under organizationResultsOverviewRoot): the group policy refreshes the overview by exact key and the results by prefix, like a Property's, and any command that invalidates the whole Portal family reaches them too. The editor's Linktree section (its switch, titles and every link with its texts) is one detail descendant, refetched with the plain link list after any link write. Analytics additionally nests propertyId, portalId, and time range so property teardown, portal teardown, and range-specific reads each have a usable prefix. Review & publish's read (`review`: the checks, the change list and the language rows) sits under `publicationHistory` too, so every working-copy write and every publication refreshes it, and the review route fetches it afresh on each entry. The editor's live preview of the draft or the live version (`preview`, keyed by Portal and source) sits under `publicationHistory`, which every working-copy write already invalidates, so the preview follows the draft as it autosaves; The Share tab's print kit read (`printKit`: the languages, titles and look the live version carries) sits under `publicationHistory`, so every publication refreshes it, and it describes the live version, so an unpublished edit does not reach a print; the download is a mutation that changes no state the page shows. `previewCopy` is the guest copy pack of one language, outside every Portal and never invalidated. The History tab's reads (the merged ledger, one infinite read per filter, and the versions with each version opened for viewing or making live again) are detail descendants, so any Portal detail refresh reaches them. Making a version live again invalidates the detail, the property list and the overview, and a version's preview is never reused: it is read fresh on each opening, because what would change depends on what is live then. The page of a version (`versionPreview`, the History's "View") is a descendant of that version, so a restore or any Portal detail refresh reaches it; it is read fresh on each opening too, because it draws only the addresses and images guests would be served now. The Property look's batch "Review & publish" reads the review of every live portal of a Property together (`lookReview`, with `lookReviewOf` naming the portals read, under the property prefix): it is fetched only while the dialog is open, never kept (a review is a decision about what to publish, so each opening reads it afresh), and refreshed by every look save. A batch publish refreshes the overview, the experience and each portal's publication history, but not these reviews: the dialog shows what the publish answered, and the next opening reads them afresh anyway; a publish request that fails refreshes the same, since it may have published some of its portals.

Connection and import-job reads live under the Integration root. Volatile Google provider content has a dedicated eviction prefix and includes organizationId, connectionId, viewEpoch, accountRef where relevant, and leaseRef for authorization state so stale views cannot share provider content.

Public portal data is keyed by the complete validated route argument object, currently the public token, beneath a Guest-only root; token navigation therefore remounts and reads a distinct cache entry.

queryKeyDelegates.policy: The helper is intentionally generic over a caller-supplied QueryKey; its only production caller passes notificationKeys.head from notification-queries.ts, which owns Organization, filter, and page-size identity.

The helper is intentionally generic over a caller-supplied QueryKey; its only production caller passes notificationKeys.list from notification-queries.ts, which owns Organization, filter, and page-size identity.

The head-fetch wrapper resets only the caller-supplied history key when a refreshed head no longer reaches it; its only production caller passes notificationKeys.list from notification-queries.ts for the same Organization, filter, and page size as the head it wraps.

The mapped value comes only from affectedProjectionKeys, whose closed array is built from portalKeys.groups, portalKeys.goalSubjects, portalKeys.goalSubjectNames, portalKeys.overview, portalKeys.organizationOverview, and (by prefix, every window) portalKeys.resultsOverviewRoot for the exact Property; the organizationResultsOverviewRoot prefix is refreshed beside them, and portalKeys.groupPagesRoot (every group's page) for the exact Property.
The private cleanup callback accepts only the hook-local dashboardKeys.googlePerformance key and cancels that exact view before removing it.
The private cleanup callback accepts only the hook-local dashboardKeys.googlePerformance key and removes that exact view after cancellation.

The generic adapter accepts typed QueryKey values supplied through invalidateKeys; feature routes remain responsible for building those values from an owned shared factory, while this loop performs only the declared targeted invalidations.
The block-local queryKey alias is portalKeys.detail(portalId); it is cancelled and snapshotted before the optimistic write.
The error block recreates the same portalKeys.detail(portalId) alias, restores its snapshot, and refetches only that exact detail.

broadInvalidationExceptions.rationale: After sign-in and active-organization selection, the authenticated route context must be rebuilt before redirect; this is the sole whole-router bootstrap exception.

stateMirrorCandidates.policy: Which page the phones show: the 1-star and 5-star pair, one guest state chosen under "See every guest state", or "Try as guest". It is the manager's own choice of what to look at, not server state, is never written back, and a remount of the page is its reset boundary.
The instant the page was opened, taken once for the goal card's days left and the history's year; it is not server state and is never written back, and a remount of the route is its reset boundary.

Seeded once from initialPanel — 'reports' only when a report-outcome notification opened the dialog — and never synchronized afterwards, so the reporter's own tab choice is not overridden. The dialog body mounts per open, which is the reset boundary.

One capture of the page geometry, taken when the form mounts over the page being described; re-capturing later would picture the form rather than the bug. It is not server state, and Remove clears it outright so a later re-consent cannot resurrect a picture the reporter dropped.

One read of the browser-local recorded-error buffer, taken when the form mounts so the offer cannot change while the reporter is typing. It is not server state and is never written back; closing the dialog discards it.

Read once from this browser's seen-outcome map when the reports panel opens, so an outcome keeps its New marker for the whole visit. Per-viewer convenience only: nothing server-side reads it, and losing it can only make a marker reappear, never hide an outcome.
Seed from the issued nonce and rotate only from confirmed start-over results; route-token remount remains the reset boundary.
Seed from the loader response, then replace only with confirmed response-mutation results; route-token remount remains the reset boundary.
Seed from the issued nonce and rotate only from confirmed start-new-response results; route-token remount remains the reset boundary.
Seed from the loader response, then replace only with confirmed response-mutation results; route-token remount remains the reset boundary.
Seed from the user image and update from the finalized upload or removal interaction; the Profile route keys the page by user id and image, so a refreshed session image remounts the local snapshot.
A route callback error seeds one dismissible client banner; recovery and new discovery actions explicitly clear or replace it.
The lazy initializer constructs one client coordinator per hook lifetime; it owns cache teardown callbacks and is not server state.
The imported EMPTY object is only the initial client live-region value; mutation announcements own subsequent values.

OrganizationLogoEditor is keyed by the persisted logo, seeds its local upload/removal snapshot from that value, and restores it after failed removal; a changed server logo remounts only this editor, not the organization form.

The transfer choices the departing member is composing, keyed by responsibility. Seeded empty rather than from `outstanding`, which stays the server-owned prop the unassigned list is derived from, so a refreshed worklist can never be overwritten by a stale local copy. Submitted once and then discarded with the dialog.
Initialize from guarded localStorage (comparing unless the reader turned it off) and persist changes; like the range, this preference is intentionally global across portals.
Initialize from schema-validated localStorage and persist changes; this preference is intentionally global across portals.

One coordinator per mounted workspace, created lazily and never derived from server data; the layout keys its provider by portal id, so a coordinator (and any unsaved edit it holds) can never be reused for another portal.

Seeded once from the form's own default values, which are what the server held when the form mounted, and advanced only by a write the server accepted; it is a comparison baseline for skipping no-op writes, not a second copy of the form's state.
The ready portals the manager unticked in the open dialog; a choice that exists only while the dialog is open, never written to the server, and reset by closing it.

Whether the open dialog is reviewing, publishing or showing what a publish did, with the outcomes the server answered; those outcomes are the answer of one request, not a copy of a read, and closing the dialog discards them.

Seeded once from the Brand Profile the page opened with; later refreshes (every save invalidates the experience read) never overwrite what the manager is editing, and a write the server accepted only advances the comparison baseline. Leaving the page is the reset boundary.

Seeded once from the Property's default languages the page opened with and advanced only by the manager's own add, remove or make-fallback; a refresh never reorders them under the manager. Leaving the page is the reset boundary.

Seeded once from the photograph and logo the page opened with and advanced only by the answer of this page's own accepted write (a focal point moved, a photograph or logo put on or taken off), which carries the media as a page draws it; a later refresh of the experience read never overwrites a focal point still being dragged. Leaving the page is the reset boundary.

Seeded once from the photograph's saved focal point when the dialog opens (the middle for a new file) and advanced only by the manager's own drag or arrow key; the dialog body is mounted only while it is open, so closing it is the reset boundary and nothing is written until Use photo or Save.

Seeded once from the descriptions the Property has saved when the dialog opens and advanced only by the manager's typing (and emptied when a new file is chosen, because the old description was about the old photograph); a refresh of the experience read never overwrites it, and nothing is written until Use photo or Save.
One idempotency key per setup session for the batch consent command; a retry reuses it so a ceremony that committed replays instead of repeating, and a remount mints a new one.

Seeded once from the setup facts the step opened with (country-suggested reply languages, the importing admin as manager); later refreshes never overwrite in-progress answers, and leaving the import route is the reset boundary.

Freezes the first ready setup facts for the session and never synchronizes: saving invalidates the property, manager and AI caches, and the refreshed facts would otherwise withdraw the answered questions and results from under the merchant. Leaving the import route is the reset boundary.
The lazy Date initializer is a client clock tick used only to keep the visible retrieval age current; report data remains owned by the query result.
The lazy Date.now value is a client clock tick used only to render a retry countdown.
An effect reconciles new normalized server assignments against the prior server selection while preserving independent local edits.
Seed from the current authorization or notice defaults and retain local capability edits until a command result replaces them; the propertyId-keyed remount prevents drafts crossing properties.

Seed from the property's snapshot and replace with confirmed command results; every caller keys MerchantAiPropertyAuthorization by propertyId (and the property AI section also by state version), so changing property or a confirmed command from elsewhere creates a fresh snapshot owner.

Whether the property section shows its own editor. Seeded from whether the property has a stored override and moved only by the reader's own two buttons; the stored override itself is read from the query result on every render, and clearing it goes through the mutation, so this holds no server value.
Seed from persisted end time and keep input local until Save; NotificationsCategoryRow keys the editor by category and persisted start/end, so a changed server window remounts the draft.
Seed from persisted start time and keep input local until Save; NotificationsCategoryRow keys the editor by category and persisted start/end, so a changed server window remounts the draft.

Starts empty and holds only the values requested for a row while that row's saves are in flight, so the next edit builds on them and the control reflects the click; the entry is removed when the row's last save settles, after the mutation's refetch, leaving the preferences query as the only render source.

The lazy initializer constructs one page-lifetime serial runner that orders each preference row's saves; it holds only in-flight save promises, never a server-owned record, and the preferences query stays the authority.
Seed from current responsibility and preserve edits for this modal instance; closing the modal unmounts the draft.
Seed from current supporting responsibilities and preserve edits for this modal instance; closing the modal unmounts the draft.

A minute-granularity wall clock: the lazy initializer reads the mounting instant and a 60 s interval advances it only while the target is active and the caller supplied no clock. It holds no server-owned record — the deadline itself comes from the response-target payload and is only formatted against this value.

The half-typed internal note, with the id of the item it belongs to. Client-only and never server-seeded: an internal note does not exist server-side until `addInboxNote` files it, so there is no server record this could go stale against, and no server read owns it. It lives above the composer's Reply / Note segment. That was originally because the segment is a Radix tab set whose inactive panel Radix unmounts, which destroyed the words on a glance at the reply box (the PR 3 defect); both panels are force-mounted now (`reply-composer.tsx`), so the mode switch no longer tears the form down and that is no longer the reason. What this still carries is a change of SELECTION, which rebuilds the item-keyed form. `InboxNotesThread` reads it once as `defaultValues` and mirrors every keystroke back through `onDraftChange`; the form owns the live value while mounted. `itemId` fences it to the selection it was typed about, so a change of selection seeds the next form empty rather than filing one item's words against another's revision, and a filed note clears both copies.

stateMirrorCandidates.owner: Inbox mobile detail sheet exit animation
stateMirrorCandidates.policy: A one-frame copy of the `item` prop, advanced during render whenever a non-null item differs from the copy, and read only when `item` is null. It is not a server authority and never outlives the prop: dismissal drops `itemId` from the search, so `item` goes null in the same commit `open` goes false, and returning null on `item` alone tore the Radix dialog out of the tree while it was still open — the closing sheet had nothing left to animate. This holds the last item just long enough for the exit, and a reopen overwrites it before anything renders. A ref cannot do the job (`react-hooks/refs` forbids both the write and the read, and the exit frame is a render that has to see the old item); an effect is too late, because the null render has already committed.
Seed from the durable reply and keep edits local until save or cancel unmounts the editor.
An effect intentionally copies the latest input after delayMs; this is a timed client projection, not server authority.

stateMirrorCandidates.owner: Inbox detail pane composer caret request
stateMirrorCandidates.policy: A request counter — `{ itemId, mode, seq }` — meaning "put the caret in this composer surface of this item", raised by the `r` / `n` shortcuts and by the thread's Edit actions. It holds no server-owned record of any kind: `seq` is a monotonic tally of asks, `mode` names a client surface and `itemId` names the selection that asked. A counter rather than a flag because a latched boolean fires its effect only on the rising edge, which would let each shortcut work exactly once per mounted pane; `seq: 0` is the initial "nobody has asked". `itemId` is what keeps a change of selection from stealing the caret, and it is load-bearing rather than descriptive: the two consuming effects (`reply-status-view.tsx`, `inbox-notes-thread.tsx`) are keyed by item and fire on MOUNT whenever the counter they are handed is non-zero, so a `seq === 0` early-return alone does not bound them — the pane outlives the selection change, and without the fence one `r` followed by a `j` down the list handed the caret to the next item's reply box and autosaved the following keystrokes onto a review nobody had opened. The reader (`caretFor`) therefore hands a surface `seq` only while `itemId` matches the current item, and `0` otherwise.

stateMirrorCandidates.owner: Inbox detail pane reply edit target
stateMirrorCandidates.policy: Which reply editor the pane has opened ('published', else null) plus the status of the rejected-to-draft reopen round trip. 'published' is now the only target: a 'rejected' one was unreachable, because `useActionMutation` awaits the write-through patch that lands `status: 'draft'` before `mutateAsync` resolves, so the reply has already re-resolved to `compose` by the time the pane could raise it. It holds no reply field: the reply itself stays server-owned in the detail query, and the editors seed their text from that payload, never from here. `itemId` records the selection this target was raised on, so a different item rebases to a closed editor rather than carrying one over. The rendered target is `liveEditTarget(replyView.kind, target)`, which is derived from the server's current reply status on every render, so a republish or a reopen closes the editor without this state being written back.
The lazy initializer constructs one component-lifetime transition observer used to reconcile polled and locally confirmed status changes; it contains no server-owned record or durable product state.

Latch the first successful list page's viewedUpTo value for the active organization and ignore later visit-stamp refetches, so rows that were new when the workspace opened keep their marker for that visit. An organization change clears the rendered value immediately and the reconciliation effect seeds the new organization's first page; the query result remains the server authority for every other list field.
The lazy initializer constructs one client autosave coordinator per mounted composer and updates its save callback through an effect.
The composite is a client-only coordinator status initialized to idle and advanced by autosave callbacks.
Seed from the durable reply draft and derived language, then keep writer edits local while autosave persists snapshots.
The lazy initializer derives a starting language from saved review/reply inputs; composer detection and adoption transitions own later values.
Seed provenance from the saved draft and update it only through composer adoption/edit transitions.
Seed from saved/property/review language inputs and preserve the writer's selection throughout the mounted composer.

The lazy Date.now initializer reads the mounting instant and a one-second interval advances it until the retry time the server returned. The consumer is keyed by that retry time, so a new busy answer is a new countdown; the value only formats 'Try again in Ns' and holds no server-owned record.
The selection stores its originating filter scope; a changed scope renders an empty selection and the setter rebases future ids onto the current scope.

Which edges of a horizontally scrolling inbox strip (the queue strip, the active-filters row) have pills out of reach, measured from the DOM on every render, on scroll and on resize. It only decides whether the strip draws an edge fade, holds no server-owned record, and returns the previous object while the answer is unchanged so scrolling does not re-render each frame.
defaultOpen seeds uncontrolled client UI state; controlled openProp remains the render authority when supplied.

Seeded once from the optional `initial` draft, which only previews and stories pass (a live page starts the note closed), and never synchronized afterwards, so the guest's own open and close is not overridden. The note composer mounts once per response, which is the reset boundary. The note's words are the form's own state (`immersive-note-form.tsx`), not this one.

Seeded once from the optional `yourResponse.initialOpen`, which only previews and stories pass (a live page starts "Your response" closed), and never synchronized afterwards, so the guest's own open and close is not overridden. The after-rating layout mounts once per rated response, which is the reset boundary. Whether the rating form is open under "Change your rating" is derived from the response's `correctedAt`, not stored as a copy of it.

The instant the page reads its deadlines against: seeded from the server's `servedAt` so the server render and the first browser render match, then advanced by the time the page has been open and re-read whenever a response arrives, so a deadline that passed while the guest read the page shows as ended. It is not server state and is never written back; unmounting the page is its reset boundary.

The current instant, read once on mount and refreshed on a one-minute interval so "2 h ago" does not go stale on a tab left open. It is not server state and is never written back; unmounting the tab is its reset boundary.

Seeded once from the editor's active section (the private note is only drawn after a low rating) and again, during render, when the active section changes to one the chosen guest state does not draw; otherwise it is the manager's own choice in the filmstrip. It is not server state and is never written back; a remount of the pane is its reset boundary.

The editor section the guest state was last aligned to, held so the alignment happens once per section change (the documented adjust-state-during-render pattern). It is never written back, and a remount of the pane is its reset boundary.

Seeded once from startsOpen (open when the property has no wording for the language yet) and never synchronized afterwards, so the manager's own open or closed choice is not overridden when a save lands; the note above it reads the wording directly.
A measurement of the strip's scroll position and size, updated from its scroll and resize events; it is never derived from or written to server data.

classificationDefinitions.server_draft: Editable local draft initialized from server-owned input; later server refreshes intentionally do not overwrite in-progress edits unless the row policy says otherwise.
classificationDefinitions.server_snapshot: Local server-derived snapshot advanced from mutation responses. The row policy names how it is refreshed and any remaining remount or reconciliation dependency.
classificationDefinitions.synchronized_prop_copy: Local copy of an input with an explicit synchronization or delay policy.
classificationDefinitions.client_persistence: Client-owned state initialized from browser persistence or another client-only preference source.
classificationDefinitions.local_runtime: Local runtime/controller state caught by the conservative syntax heuristic; it is not treated as a server-state authority.

limitations: This executable inventory covers production TypeScript and TSX files under src/components, src/routes, src/hooks, and src/shared/hooks; it excludes tests, stories, context internals, workers, and external packages.

The state-mirror inventory is a conservative syntax heuristic over non-literal useState initializers. It requires unique, current, owned classifications and rejects an effect that overwrites a declared server draft, but feature-owned tests must still prove each remount, conflict, synchronization, or mutation-adoption policy.

The query-key check rejects direct array literals, requires every factory member to descend acyclically from its own unique family root, inventories every member against an owned lifecycle policy, requires every explicit or shorthand queryKey site to resolve to a registered factory member or a narrow documented generic delegate, and requires every useActionMutation invalidation array to resolve to owned factory keys. It still does not prove that every server read uses TanStack Query or that every mutation invalidates all semantically related sibling projections; those fan-outs need feature-owned behavioral tests such as the Portal Group to Goal cache matrix.
The invalidation check detects zero-argument .invalidate() calls in scope. The login auth-bootstrap row is the only approved whole-router exception.
